meaning.text: Expected time in the queue is roughly the product of three factors: how busy the server is, how variable the work is, and how long each item takes.
The text calls it Kingman's approximation and uses it to separate the three things that make you wait.

spans.text: Expected value (E[·]) of W_q. W_q is not defined in the surrounding text, which frames the formula as the time you wait.
Coefficients of variation of the time between arrivals and of the service time.

items.text: ρ/(1 − ρ), the utilization factor: it grows without bound as ρ approaches 1, so a nearly full server makes the wait explode.
(c_a² + c_s²)/2, the variability factor: the average of the two squared coefficients of variation; it is 0 when neither arrivals nor service vary.
t_s scales the product to the mean service time, so the wait is measured in the same unit as the work.

spans.text: An approximation for a single server under heavy load; at low utilization it overstates the wait.
